A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Polynomial Stein Discrepancy (PSD) work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix reorganization.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original goodness-of-fit simulations, SGLD tuning results and runtime measurements. Appendix B reports additional asymptotic-test experiments.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, and Appendix C adds logistic-regression simulations, moment-tracking studies, interaction ablations and translation-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Appendix C.7 adds an evaluated mean-centred PSD variant using x minus the mean of Q. The polynomial objective, Stein operator and bootstrap/asymptotic tests remain unchanged. Interaction-free PSD and invertible linear transformations were already described in v1.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds sparse-prior and approximately Gaussian logistic-regression tasks, correctly specified and misspecified Rosenbrock targets, and a contaminated Gaussian sequence with nonconvergent second moments. These substantially broaden the evaluated distributions and Bayesian inference settings.

E2.justification: The original external comparators—IMQ KSD, Gauss KSD, FSSD-opt and RFSD—are retained. New comparisons include interaction-free PSD in the existing SGLD setting, mean-centred PSD, and Euclidean distances to true or gold-standard moments as oracle references.

E3.justification: New protocols include ULA step-size sweeps, normalized discrepancies and Euclidean moment-error comparisons, Rosenbrock sample-size trajectories, and translation tests with N=100 and d=5. The original goodness-of-fit sample sizes, significance level and bootstrap settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C.2–C.7 add direct moment-tracking diagnostics, interaction-removal ablations for SGLD and logistic regression, correlated-covariate checks, a non-Gaussian failure analysis and mean-translation sensitivity tests. v1's supplementary empirical analysis principally compared asymptotic and bootstrap testing.

E5.justification: The new logistic-regression studies report five-run summaries and normalized median discrepancies; the translation study specifies 200 independent simulations. Original repetition counts are retained. No new confidence intervals or uncertainty bands accompany these additions.

E6.justification: Original benchmark outcomes, including Table 1, are retained. Tables 2–4 and Figures 6–12 add substantial results: sparse-logistic PSD with r≥2 selects step size 0.005 while KSD minimizes at 0.1; higher-order PSD selects 0.0005 in the big-data example. Additional findings concern interaction removal, translation sensitivity and Rosenbrock moment tracking.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds a Lagrange-multiplier derivation of the existing closed form, and Appendix C.6 derives zero-PSD conditions for the Rosenbrock target. The main moment-matching proof and invertible-transform corollary are retained. Proposition 1 now states its Gaussian assumption explicitly.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction express the guarantee directly for Gaussian targets instead of primarily through the Bernstein–von Mises limit. The conclusion emphasizes detecting moment discrepancies. The central contributions of linear-time PSD, goodness-of-fit testing and sampler tuning remain intact.

C2.justification: The conclusion and appendices substantially expand applicability boundaries: undefined moments, discrepancies above the chosen polynomial order, lost correlation detection without interactions, translation sensitivity and non-Gaussian relationships between moments. They also introduce a gradient-linearity heuristic. The specific Rosenbrock interpretation has an internal inconsistency concerning its b-only perturbation.

D1.justification: New studies disclose prior scales, simulated-data dimensions, sparsity, step-size grids and transformation constructions. The existing code reference and single-core cluster disclosure are retained. Sampler lengths and construction of the logistic-regression gold-standard moments remain insufficiently documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning relative to Liu and Wang's moment-matching work and explains how PSD differs from conventional polynomial-kernel KSD. It expands discussion of Kanagawa et al.'s moment-controlling KSD and adds references supporting the Gaussian approximation and new experimental examples.

P1.justification: There are targeted wording changes, corrected figure references, an expanded conclusion and an added impact statement. References move before the appendices, which are reorganized into A–D. Most background, method exposition and original experimental narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 6–12 and Tables 2–4 add moment-error trajectories, posterior contour comparisons, interaction-ablation plots and translation-power results. Original displays are largely retained, with a small title/layout edit to Figure 3. The visual evidence is substantially expanded.

improvement.justification: v2 improves practical validation through direct moment-error comparisons, logistic-regression studies and interaction/translation analyses, while explaining applicability more fully than v1. The gain is limited by incomplete sampler and gold-standard details and a new inconsistency in Appendix C.6: changing only b in its displayed Rosenbrock family preserves the stated zero-PSD1 moment identities, contrary to the claimed non-vanishing behavior.
